title: CSV import pipeline
description: Server-side CSV import for apps: upload, preview with suggested column mapping, per-row validation with typed parsers and in-file duplicate checks, idempotent commit through your own save function, and a formula-safe error report, with tenant/user scoping and a Fetch Request/Response adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, crypto.randomUUID, structuredClone, TextEncoder/TextDecoder and the Fetch Request/Response and ReadableStream APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Declare the importable fields: key, label, required, aliases, parse ('string', 'integer', 'decimal', 'boolean', 'date', 'email' or a custom function), unique and maxLength.
Implement ImportStore on your database with a conditional status update (UPDATE ... WHERE id = $1 AND status = $2) and a scheduled delete of expired imports.
Implement onRow(record, rowNumber) to save one record, idempotently keyed on importId and rowNumber, with your own unique constraints; throw to record a row failure.
Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token, returning tenantId and userId; never from the request body.
Set parser limits (maxBytes, maxRows, maxColumns, maxFieldLength) and the HTTP maxUploadBytes to what your app accepts.
Mount createImportHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy.
limitations: Does not save records; onRow does, and cross-file or database uniqueness must be enforced there.
UTF-8 text only; no Excel (.xlsx), other encodings or streaming of files larger than the in-memory caps (default 5 MiB, 10,000 rows).
Dates must be ISO YYYY-MM-DD and decimals parse to JavaScript numbers; use a custom parser for local formats or exact money.
A process crash during commit leaves the import in committing; recover it from your store using the saved progress and your idempotent onRow.
The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only. No rate limiting; add request limits (see the rate-limit module) to the upload route.
Production database correctness, session security and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: upload is the raw text/csv body (not multipart), UTF-8 only; other types → 415
limits 5 MiB, 10,000 rows, 200 columns → 413; staged imports expire after 24 h
commit saves only valid rows and is repeat-safe; not-validated or commit-in-progress → 409

behaviors: RFC 4180 quotes, escaped quotes, embedded line breaks, CRLF/CR/LF and a UTF-8 BOM parse correctly; malformed quoting is rejected
the delimiter is detected among comma, semicolon, tab and pipe, ignoring quoted text
byte (UTF-8), row, column and field-length caps are enforced
column mapping is suggested case-, punctuation- and accent-insensitively with aliases, each header used once
integer, decimal, boolean, date, email and custom parsers accept valid and reject invalid values with distinct codes
missing required columns and empty required cells are reported; rows with extra cells are invalid
repeated values in unique fields are reported with the rows involved
a second commit returns the first result without calling onRow again; a concurrent commit gets commit-in-progress
a failed onRow records a row error without exposing its message and the commit continues
another user's or tenant's import id and expired imports read as not-found
the error report prefixes cells starting with = + - @ TAB or CR with an apostrophe
HTTP adapter: status codes, 401, origin check, media type, upload size cap, non-UTF-8 refusal and no-store headers

changes: First release: RFC 4180 parser, importer core, in-memory store and Fetch adapter.
